content.text: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/740
PR-740 has been merged into the master branch.
1) I'm having trouble rebasing the Java 8 branch past this patch. The test added by
uses JCR properties with a "_ref" suffix, and it's not at all clear to me what they are for or how they should be handled.
2) I cannot find any "IndirectContainer example" in the document linked.
3) Is this issue actually a question of LDP compliance/support, or is Fedora 4 taking special pains to support helpful behaviors for one particular data model?
The IndirectContainer example is on the second and third pages.
As far as I know, this is the behavior that is indicated in the LDP spec.
The *_ref properties are from a mock in a unit test; I believe they were used to guarantee that there wasn't a built-in expectation of property URIs.
Thanks
, but I'm still not with you. Are you referring to the text that begins "Instead the Proxy is POSTed to an IndirectContainer" or to something else?
The "_ref" properties are indeed mocks in the unit test that
added: can you clarify what you mean by "a built-in expectation of property URIs"? Are you talking about the JCR names of properties?
Yes- language of Proxy aside, the action there is a completely unremarkable example of using an IndirectContainer.
The reason for the _ref URIs in the mock is to test the insertion for references to arbitrary properties; the suffix comes from:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/utils/FedoraTypesUtils.java#L48
and it's inserted by:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/utils/FedoraTypesUtils.java#L258
Thanks,
, for helping
with the explanation.

I'm even more confused now. If we're currently testing this functionality using knowledge of the internal workings of the component under test in order to prove a workflow that is defined by an outside spec, then shouldn't this have been an integration test to begin with?
There is also an integration test. Andrew added a unit test at my request. Is the unit test failing in your rebase? Do you see ways in which the mocking could be done at a higher level?
The unit test
is

failing, but more importantly, I don't perceive the need for it. The class under test cannot alone fulfill the workflow to which we've referred. It seems to me that the only meaningful test is the integration test...

I think there is a need for some kind of unit testing here, although looking again at the changeset I could see refactoring the private function there to be viewable to package tests might be preferable. Do you want to mark that test with Ignore and open a ticket for a minor refactor? Do you want to re-open this ticket?

Given that this is a pending branch (the Java 8 branch) and not some pressing open ticket-branch, I'm willing to @Ignore it for now and reopen this ticket, which can become part of the punchlist for the Java 8 move.
Reopened for Java 8: see discussion for rationale.

This ticket addresses a very specific bug, namely, prior to the PR associated with this ticket LDP Indirect Containers did not work in F4. That bug has been fixed and merged with the master branch. When we release 4.1.1 next week, this JIRA ticket will be included (unless we want to roll back the bug fix).
If the unit tests are not working in the Java8 branch, I would suggest creating a new ticket to that effect, and moving this current ticket back to "closed".
Okay, that's more clear.
Moved reopening to FCREPO-1398.
This task is to walk through the IndirectContainer example here:
https://docs.google.com/a/fedora-commons.org/document/d/1RI8aX8XQEk-30-Ht-DaPF5nz_VtI1-eqxUuDvF3nhv0/edit#
...ensuring that the "/collections/{id}" container is updated with member statements.
Currently it is not.
